model_reported.name: evaluer-performances
model_reported.summary: Recorded the measured parent and baseline for context, without claiming a result for the unmeasured candidate.

memory_lessons.applicability: The current parent using a 1024-CTA cap was correct on all 10 reported cases and measured 0.4474 ms mean; that result does not isolate the cap's effect or establish that fewer CTAs will be faster.
memory_lessons.claim: The selected single-kernel parent is valid across the reported sizes and seeds, but its performance provides no evidence yet about a smaller CTA cap.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this 256-CTA cap under the same protocol, including output reset and launch overhead, and compare correctness and timing with the parent.

proposal.hypothesis: Reducing the large-input grid cap from 1024 to 256 limits output atomics to at most 256 per call while preserving one input pass and the per-call reset. This may reduce contention, but it may also reduce memory-level parallelism; the controller should compare total time including reset and launch overhead and validate every required size and the FP64 tolerance.

retained: Keep the asynchronous per-call output reset and the one-pass input reduction with one CTA atomicAdd.
Reduce the large-input grid cap from 1024 CTAs to 256; retain ceil(n/256) blocks for smaller inputs.
